question: A student on academic warning wants to drop one course to have a more manageable load, which would bring their total enrolled units from 36 to 27. Is this straightforward, and what are the consequences?
expected_answer: This is not straightforward. Dropping from 36 to 27 units would make the student part-time (below 36 units), which requires an exception from the Associate Dean for Education. Without that exception, going part-time would itself trigger additional academic consequences. Students on academic warning face this bind: they cannot overload to take more courses, and going below 36 units without approval creates new problems. The advisor should be consulted before any action.
reasoning_type: Policy interaction — academic action + full-time/part-time rules
common_mistake: Treating dropping as a simple administrative step without recognizing the full-time status implications; not connecting the 36-unit full-time threshold with the academic action policy
needs_verification: Confirm the full-time threshold is 36 units at CMU-Q
Confirm that going below 36 units without Dean approval triggers additional academic consequences
Confirm whether the Academic Warning status changes the standard advice for dropping courses
